answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, transferable stake before it can submit bids; the protocol samples a timber, quartz, or sable job at random, and a missed deadline burns part of that stake while successful work earns fees. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply influence for free: each needs its own capital, and an attacker who spreads stake across fake agents risks repeated penalties when those agents fail audits or cannot deliver. The cost is tied to identities and persists even when they are discarded.
